subject: Packaging recommendation: Slim vs Full recommendation and approvals
messages:
From: Emma Saunders <emma@stellara.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Stellara AI Procurement <procurement@stellara.ai>; David Lee <david.lee@stellara.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Packaging: looking for guidance on upgrade options and discounts

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team liked the latency numbers and the commit math looks promising. We're trying to map two internal scenarios to a Redwood package and could use a succinct recommendation:

1) "Slimline" — maintain current consumption profile, add only inference caching + 50% more tokens (short-sequence optimization). Minimal new features, lower monthly commit.

2) "FullStack" — larger commitment to get Dedicated capacity, priority routing, and the full Optimize suite (batching recommendations + eval alerts). Higher commit, lower per-token price, includes SSO + longer retention.

Can you:
- Recommend which package aligns to a 6–12 month adoption plan for a data-heavy pilot (20–30M tokens/mo peak)?
- Share the typical uplift in discount we can expect moving from Slimline -> FullStack (ballpark percent and what approvals are required).
- Confirm what items would be add-ons vs included for each package.

Also, procurement wants to know what supporting docs you can attach (service matrix, feature list, standard SOW). If possible please attach a short comparison PDF.

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Saunders
Head of ML Platform, Stellara AI
emma@stellara.ai

Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging: looking for guidance on upgrade options and discounts

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear summary. TL;DR below, full details attached (proposal + feature matrix).

Options (short):
• Slimline upgrade — what it includes:
  - Incremental token commit (20–30M token block)
  - Prefix/KV caching enabled, short-sequence kernel tuning
  - Email support, monthly performance review
  - Pricing: per-token drops ~8–12% vs current hosted tiers; no Dedicated capacity
  - Add-ons: SSO, extended retention, Optimize advanced rules (charged separately)

• FullStack upgrade — what it includes:
  - Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool), predictable throughput
  - Priority routing + guaranteed failover window
  - Redwood Optimize (batching & eval alerts) + 90-day retention
  - Pricing: per-token drops ~20–28% vs current hosted tiers depending on commit; some features that are add-ons in Slimline are bundled here

Recommendation: For a 6–12 month data-heavy pilot where predictable latency under load matters, FullStack is a stronger fit — it avoids noisy-neighbor variance and gives you the toolset to tune unit economics. If the pilot is exploratory and you want to limit spend while validating model performance, start Slimline and set a committed step-up after 2 months (we can auto-validate based on latency and token thresholds).

Discount/Approval notes:
- Up to 15% list discount on Slimline can be approved by regional AE (Marcus).
- Any total contract discount >15% or with a multi-year commit needs manager/finance approval (Aditya signs off for deals >20% or nonstandard T&Cs).
- Formal enterprise addenda (SOC2/KMS) may cause an operations surcharge that reduces net discount.

Attachments included: proposal_slimline-vs-fullstack.pdf, service_matrix.xlsx (feature/retention/vendor requirements).

Next steps:
1) If you want pricing for specific commit levels, share a target token/month and desired retention window.
2) If FullStack, we can prepare a technical runbook + Dedicated sizing session and a draft SOW.

Happy to jump on a 30m call with procurement + infra to walk through the tradeoffs — what times work this week?

Best,
Mina Haddad

Mina — parsed the ask. Pricing guidance and approvals below so you can respond to procurement quickly.

Quick numbers (ballpark, list pricing normalized):
- Slimline (commit 25M tokens/mo): list $8,500/mo -> AE price $7,650/mo (10% off)
- FullStack (commit 30M tokens/mo + Dedicated baseline): list $22,000/mo -> AE price $17,600/mo (20% off)

Discount policy:
- I can approve up to 15% off list for Slimline in my quota.
- For FullStack, 20% is within standard manager approval; for anything beyond 22% we need CS and Finance acknowledgement (OpEx impact + capacity booking).

Notes on concessions: 
- If procurement asks for seat credits or extended trial periods, prefer to structure as a technical onboarding credit (one-time) rather than permanent percent off.
- Include a renewal step-down clause in the SOW so we can revisit unit economics at year 1.

If you want, I can draft a short approval email for Aditya to sign (I've pre-approved up to 20% pending their final signoff).

-Marcus
